prompt: You must recommend the board approve a cost-reduction program to protect margin amid rising input costs. Write the storyline, leading with the recommendation.
context: Input costs (key raw material) have risen 19% year-over-year (public commodity index, referenced internally). The company has not raised prices in 14 months due to competitive positioning concerns. Finance has identified three cost levers: (1) procurement consolidation across suppliers, estimated $4.2M/year savings, 6-month implementation; (2) manufacturing footprint consolidation (closing one of four plants), estimated $7.8M/year savings, 14-month implementation, requires workforce reduction; (3) SG&A reduction across corporate functions, estimated $2.5M/year savings, 3-month implementation. A customer-pricing study (completed) suggests a targeted 3-4% price increase on the top 2 product lines would be absorbed by the market with minimal volume loss.

binaryCriteria.description: Includes the evidenced 3-4% targeted price increase as part of the recommendation, not only cost-cutting levers, since the pricing study directly supports it.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the price-increase option is omitted from the recommendation despite being directly evidenced in the context.

binaryCriteria.description: Treats manufacturing footprint consolidation (workforce reduction, 14-month timeline) as a distinct, higher-stakes decision requiring its own explicit discussion, not bundled at the same urgency as the other levers.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if plant consolidation is recommended with the same immediacy/ease as SG&A reduction or procurement consolidation without flagging its distinct risk profile.

binaryCriteria.description: Recommends the fastest, lowest-risk levers (price increase, SG&A reduction) as near-term actions ahead of the longest/highest-risk lever (plant consolidation).
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the storyline does not differentiate timing/risk across the three cost levers.

goldNotes: A strong storyline leads with a combined recommendation (not cost-cutting alone): pursue the targeted 3-4% price increase (fastest, revenue-positive, and directly evidenced by the completed pricing study) alongside the fastest-to-implement, lowest-risk cost lever (SG&A reduction, 3 months) as near-term actions, while treating plant consolidation ($7.8M, 14 months, workforce reduction) as a separate, higher-stakes decision requiring its own explicit board discussion given its scale and people impact — not bundled automatically into a single "approve all cost levers" ask. A weak storyline either ignores the pricing-increase option entirely (treating this as a pure cost-cutting problem when the data explicitly supports a revenue lever too) or recommends plant consolidation with the same urgency/ease as the other levers without flagging its distinct risk profile (workforce reduction, longest timeline).
